description: Pre-review self-audit for a skill's evals and smoke-tests, catching recurring defect classes before the reviewer fan-out.

evals.name: Review a smoke_test.py with a zero-match vacuous assertion
evals.prompt:
Here is a check function from a skill's scripts/smoke_test.py. Review it per your Check 1 (assertion non-vacuity) and report any defect found.

```python
def check_examples_documented():
    text = open('SKILL.md').read()
    matches = re.findall(r'references/\*\.md', text)
    for m in matches:
        if 'example' not in m:
            return False, 'missing example reference'
    return True, 'all example references present'
```

(Note: this target skill has no references/ directory at all, so the regex `references/\*\.md` never matches anything in a real SKILL.md.)
evals.expected_output: Flags this as a vacuous assertion under the zero-match-guard defect class: the check iterates over re.findall results that are always empty (since the literal pattern references/\*\.md never appears verbatim in prose), so the loop body never executes and the function always returns True/PASS regardless of the actual skill's state.

evals.name: Review an evals.json with a coverage-claim mismatch
evals.expected_output: Flags the coverage-claim mismatch: declared_scenarios_covered is claimed as 3 (matching declared_scenarios_total, with an empty uncovered list) but only 1 eval exists, exercising only 1 of the 3 declared scenarios — the other 2 ('converting a slash command', 'improving an existing skill') should appear in uncovered but don't.

uncovered: check_evals.py's coverage arithmetic rejects a negative declared_scenarios_total/declared_scenarios_covered
